0.1 This Indian Standard ( Part 5 ) was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 19 March 1987, after the draft finalized by the Printed Circuits Sectional Committee had been approved by the Electronics and Telecommunication Division Council. 0.2 This standard ( Part 5 ) is to be used in conjunction with IS : 5921 ( Part 1 )-1983" which is a necessary adjunct to this standard. 0.3 While preparing following: this standard, assistance has been derived from the

6. ELECTRICAL PROPERTIES 6.1 The electrical Table 1. properties shall meet the requirements as given in

7. NON-ELECTRICAL SHEET

PROPERTIES OF THE COPPER-CLAD

7.1 Surface Finish of the Copper-Clad Face 7.1.1 The copper-clad face shall be substantially free from blisters, wrinkles, pinholes, deep scratches, pits and resin. Any discolouration or contamination shall be readily removed with a hydrochloric acid solution of density 1'02 g/cm3 or with a suitable organic solvent. The surface shall be inspected in accordance with 6.2 of IS : 5921 ( Part 1 )1983". The surface finish of the copper-clad face shall be such as not to conceal imperfactions. 7.1.2 The surface of the copper foil shall be free from scratches of depth greater than 0'010 mm or l/5 of the nominal thickness of the copper foil, whichever is the lower. 7.1.3 The total length of scratches of depth greater than 0'005 mm but not greater than 0'010 mm shall not exceed 1 m per square metre of the total area of the sheet under test. 7.1.4 The area of any one or number of pinholes in an area of 0'5 m2 shall not exceed the area of a circle of diameter 0'125 mm. 7.1.5 No sheet shall have more imperfections of the types listed than those permitted by Table 2.

7.4 Solderability 7.6.1 When the sheet is tested as specified in 6.8 of IS : 5921 ( Part I)1983* and in accordance with the times and temperatures specified below, the soldered areas shall be covered with a smooth and bright solder coating. Scattered imperfections, such as, pin-holes, shall not occur on more than 5 percent of the surface and shall not be concentrated in one area. At least six specimens out of each batch of ten shall pass the test. a) Wetting

NON-ELECTRICAL PROPERTIES OF THE BASE MATERIAL AFTER COMPLETE REMOVAL OF THE COPPER FOIL

8.1 Appearance of the Base Material - The base material shall be substantially free El-om pits, holes, scratches, porosity and resin inclusions and substantially uniform in colour. A small amount of irregular variation of colour is permissible. 8.2 Flexural Strengfh - This test is applicable to sheets not thinner than 1'0 mm of nominai thickness. The test should be carried out in accordance with7.1 of IS : 5921 (Part 1 )-1983*. The flexural strength shall not be less than 11 000 N/cm2.

4 No specimen shall burn with flaming combustion for more than
